takeaways.label: Record H1 profitability on defense mix
takeaways.text: H1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹120 cr at a 27.4% margin and PAT of ₹57 cr at 13% are the highest ever in absolute terms and margins, driven by a favorable domestic defense production mix and operating expense control.

takeaways.label: ₹2,036 cr order inflow, led by radars
takeaways.text: Incremental Q2 inflows included ₹1,967 cr from radar orders, headlined by the ₹1,844 cr Uttam AAU contract from HAL; management sees clear visibility to book another ₹1,200 cr in FY27.

takeaways.label: Space demerger unlocks hidden value
takeaways.text: Every Astra shareholder will receive one share of Astra Space Technologies Ltd (ASTL) at no cost, a business management argues already owns a two-decade ISRO-qualified moat that new investors would have to price and pay for separately.

takeaways.label: Margins guided 26–28% with operating leverage tailwind
takeaways.text: The fixed cost base is not expected to rise dramatically, so incremental revenue should flow disproportionately to the bottom line; management is comfortable guiding that steady-state band over the next 2–3 years.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the ₹600 cr of already-concluded orders materialize by next month as promised, progress on the Uttam AAU delivery commitment of 2 units by March 27, and any update on the BEL QRSAM main contract award timeline.

points.label: Uttam AAU anchor order
points.text: Secured a ₹1,844 cr order from HAL for the Uttam Active Array Unit; hardware for the first prototype has been delivered to DRDO, with firmware and software integration ongoing.

points.label: Delivery schedule committed
points.text: 2 units by March 27 (management is trying for 4), a contractual milestone of 12 units by March 28, scaling to ~25 units annually in FY29 and 33–34 units thereafter.

points.label: QRSAM advance-action orders in execution
points.text: Small-quantity FOPM orders received from BEL are being executed in Q3 and Q4; the main contract award from BEL is expected anytime from December to March, with Astra's contract to follow within 3–4 months, implying execution likely starting in late FY28 or FY29.

points.label: Sukhoi-30 radar and EW programs on track
points.text: Astra is a party to DRDO programs for both the radar and electronic warfare systems on the Sukhoi-30 platform; orders are expected around calendar year 2029.

points.label: FY28 consolidated order book ambition
points.text: Management is hopeful of reaching approximately ₹5,500–5,600 cr without the main QRSAM order, and crossing ₹6,000 cr with "a little bit of luck."

points.label: Longer-term order base building
points.text: An order base of roughly ₹8,000–10,000 cr is seen building over the coming years, with a substantial part already in hand.

quotes.text: Kabra: "We are moving, as we have spoken now multiple times, from building subsystems for others to owning complete systems and the IP inside them. And that's very valuable."

points.label: Counter-drone system delivered
points.text: Astra successfully realized its counter-drone radar and delivered it to DRDO for final integration and trials during the quarter; it is the only company apart from BEL to have started production and delivery from the DRDO TOT among the seven licensees.

points.label: Three own products delivered by Diwali
points.text: A complete counter-drone system (with D4 radar as the backbone), an Astra-designed bird detection radar, and a low-level lightweight radar with a demonstrated range of 25 km+ (specification ~40–50 km).

points.label: Counter-drone market and share ambition
points.text: Management described the opportunity as a "mega business" with both military and civilian sides, projecting the market at ₹3,000–5,000 cr over the next 5 years and targeting a minimum 30% share; currently offering soft kill (jammer), with hard kill under development for the years ahead.

points.label: Low-level lightweight radar visibility
points.text: At least close to ₹1,000 cr in business over the next 5 years; the company will participate in forthcoming tenders.

points.label: Bird detection radar pipeline
points.text: Overall business expected at roughly ₹200–300 cr in the next 2–3 years; the first RFP bid has already been submitted.

points.label: Electronic mines in development
points.text: A "very high potential global product" in new-age electronic mines is expected before the end of the year.

points.label: R&D pipeline advancing to trials
points.text: Small and medium-range surveillance/tracking radars, next-gen RF seekers, wideband jammers, ammunition electronics, and enhanced DWRs are in advanced stages and expected to go to field trials from next quarter onwards.

quotes.text: Kabra: "If there's a drone, there has to be a counter-drone system, right? So it's a mega business. I'm scared to put a number onto that."

points.label: Demerger mechanics
points.text: The space business is being demerged into Astra Space Technologies Limited (ASTL); every Astra shareholder will receive one ASTL share for every Astra share held at no cost.

points.label: Incumbent advantage framed as time
points.text: Management argues ASTL possesses something nobody else can buy: nearly two decades of ISRO certifications designing, building, and delivering space-qualified hardware.

points.label: ASTL revenue plan
points.text: Cumulative revenue of ₹2,250–2,500 cr is planned over the next 4 years, with annual revenue expected to reach ₹800–900 cr by FY31, excluding any global supply chain opportunities.

points.label: Year-end order book target
points.text: ASTL is expected to carry forward an order book of ₹900 cr by March 2027, which includes space and radar.

points.label: Global supply chain conversations underway
points.text: Discussions with global players are in progress; management will communicate when something tangible materializes.

quotes.text: Kabra: "Most investors who want a stake in the space economy will have to find it price it and then pay for it. Astra shareholders already own it."

points.label: All-time high gross and EBITDA margins in Q2
points.text: Driven by a favorable product mix weighted toward production orders, which enabled capture of higher EBITDA margin.

points.label: Operating leverage thesis
points.text: The fixed cost base is not expected to go up dramatically; most incremental business will flow disproportionately to the bottom line, supporting the 26–28% steady-state EBITDA margin guidance over the next 2–3 years, with upside possible if conditions improve.

points.label: Working capital improvement underway
points.text: Targeting zero CC limits and debt-free status on working capital by year-end; the cash conversion cycle target is 350 days, down from 370 days, and may go further down as the systems business increases its share.

points.label: Near debt-free target
points.text: Management aims to be near debt-free in the next 1 to 1.5 years.

points.label: Inventory buildup is deliberate
points.text: Inventory has risen versus last year because management proactively stockpiled components with increased lead times, driven by the geopolitical situation, to avoid delivery impacts even into Q1 of the next financial year.

quotes.text: Kabra: "I don't think our fixed cost base will go up dramatically, right? So there is a huge- most of the business which comes in will flow, uh, post that straight onto the bottom line."

points.label: AAS Limited H1 performance
points.text: Booked sales of ₹334 cr, bagged ₹413 cr in orders, and holds an order book of ₹913 cr; management is confident of meeting the ₹600 cr+ revenue guidance for the full year.

points.label: Near-term pipeline
points.text: More than ₹500 cr in orders is in the pipeline and expected in the next 2 quarters.

points.label: JV partner orders
points.text: Another ₹1,200–1,500 cr is expected in the next 6–8 months, with clear visibility for another ₹1,500–2,000 cr over the following year, providing good order book visibility for the next 2–3 years.

points.label: Self-reliance philosophy on IP
points.text: Management emphasized a deliberate choice to own the IP and technology inside its products rather than sourcing core products from outside and repackaging them as India-made.

points.label: Multi-decadal opportunity thesis
points.text: Astra sees itself on the cusp of a multi-decadal opportunity, with radars, EW, counter-drone systems, electro-optics, missile seekers, and electronic mines each representing substantial business lines; how much can be captured is, in management's words, a function of ambition and ability.

points.label: Technology gap closing
points.text: India's technological gap in sensors is described as "not too far away now... a matter of a year or 2" to build products ready for the international market.

points.label: MMIC export interest
points.text: Interest from US and European markets has been received; management expects this to translate into business in the next couple of years.

points.label: International go-to-market approach
points.text: First establish and demonstrate solutions in the Indian market before taking them to international customers.

points.label: Global player ambition, no roadmap yet
points.text: When asked what additional capabilities are needed to become a global defense electronics player like Elbit or Hensoldt, and whether partnerships, JVs, or acquisitions are being explored, management answered in general terms about attitudinal shift and ambition, stating there is no clear answer and acknowledging the question remains open.

quotes.text: Kabra: "I think we are limited by our ambition. Not only Astra, a few other Indian companies I can say, you know, it's a sector which is doing amazingly, poised to do amazingly well. How much we capitalize on it, that's a function of our ambition and our abilities."

items.title: HAL Uttam radar order
items.text: Astra won its largest-ever order in July 2026: 122 AAAUs and 121 interface frames for the Uttam radar from HAL, worth ₹2,205 cr including tax (~₹1,870 cr ex-GST), execution over 5 years. It roughly doubled the order book to a record ₹4,300 cr, with 2 units due by March '27, 12 by March '28, and a ramp to 33-34 units a year from FY29.

items.title: Astra Rafael Comsys SDR ramp
items.text: The JV booked ₹413 cr of orders and ₹334 cr of sales in H1 FY27, lifting its order book to ₹913 cr, and targets ₹600-700 cr revenue this year and ~₹1,000 cr next year, with ₹1,200-1,500 cr of orders expected over 6-8 months. At guided 18-20% JV EBITDA margins, this adds roughly ₹20 cr-plus of Astra's share of profit on FY27 revenue alone.

items.title: QRSAM production orders via BEL
items.text: BEL is hopeful of winning the main QRSAM contract between December and March, with Astra's subsystem orders following within 3-4 months; FOPM orders are already received and in execution. Management expects at least ₹700-800 cr more from QRSAM for the first 3 regiments beyond the existing book, with execution from Q4 FY28.

items.title: ASTL demerger and listing
items.text: The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology demerger cleared BSE and NSE observation letters on 29 Oct 2026, with listing targeted by Q1 FY28. ASTL guides to ₹300-plus cr first-year revenue at 18-20% PBT margin, ~₹800-900 cr annually by FY31, and carries a ~₹900 cr order book plus a ~₹2,000 cr weather inquiry pipeline.

items.title: Su-30 Virupaksha and Angad pipeline
items.text: Astra delivered the first Virupaksha radar AAU prototype hardware to DRDO, with radar commissioning expected next year and Su-30 production orders around calendar 2029; the Angad pod jammer qualification is due within a year. Management counts at least ₹3,000 cr of order-intake pipeline from these two Su-30 programs.

items.title: Own-branded counter-drone systems
items.text: Astra delivered its counter-drone system with the D4 radar to DRDO for final trials, demonstrated an EM wall and vehicle-mounted anti-drone system in July 2026, and projects a ₹3,000-5,000 cr market over 5 years in which it hopes for at least 30% share. Bird-detection radar (₹200-300 cr expected in 2-3 years) and low-level radar (~₹1,000 cr visibility over 5 years) add further own-product revenue.

items.title: AMCA radar AAAU win
items.text: Astra emerged L1 (with BEL as L2) for the AMCA Active Antenna Array Unit, with the contract expected within about a month as of Q1 FY27. It also sits in the supply chain for the AMCA radar whichever of the 3 shortlisted consortium partners wins.
